title: Identifying Treated Effects with Latent Binary Outcomes Observed on a Coarse Time Grid
banked_reason: Cold general referee: delivered tier subfield against required floor field; projected paper-score ceiling 6.5 < 7.4; salvageable=false. Math referee PASS.
gap_reasons: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.

The leading-journal score is constrained by the binary-state setting, transported knowledge of both emissions and coarse untreated dynamics, complete panels, one adoption opportunity per interval, and the absence of sampling theory or inference near binding feasibility constraints.

The novelty discussion also fails to compare theorem statements against the cited 2026 latent-outcome and dynamic-selection papers, leaving the closest-literature priority claim insufficiently substantiated.
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation replaced inverse bridges by existential survivor flows and proved a sharp extension characterization over the full binary stochastic-root boundary. Risk-set subtraction then identified observed-grid untreated path laws, supported path-functional mean effects, and cohort ATT, with exact twin and root-exclusion constructions. The math referee passed the package, but the cold novelty referee capped it at subfield; reaching field tier would require a distinct extension such as incomplete panels, unknown calibration, multiple opportunities, or inference.
tldr: A complete coarse-grid panel law can filter fine-time latent Markov roots even when adoption depends arbitrarily on untreated latent history.  For binary latent outcomes, one opportunity per interval, calibrated oriented emissions, and complete reports, a calibrated stochastic root extends to the full cohort/report law exactly when nonnegative survivor flows fit within the decision-state capacities and reach the observed survivor endpoints.  This finite linear feasibility characterization covers singular, reducible, and boundary roots.  Risk-set subtraction then identifies the adopters' entire untreated counterfactual path law on the observed grid, not only its endpoint mean.  Combining that law with the deconvolved factual cohort path table identifies every supported average observed-grid path-functional effect; cohort-time latent-state ATT is the principal coordinate corollary even when the fine transition remains set identified.
gap: Existing stochastic-root results characterize temporal refinements of Markov transitions, ordinary HMM results recover or test measurement models at the observation resolution, and causal latent-state methods generally invoke randomization, observed-covariate exchangeability, weighting, parallel trends, or parametric g-formula restrictions. The targeted search found no theorem deciding whether each coarse-time root extends through an arbitrary nonanticipating latent-history adoption law while reproducing the complete cohort/report distribution, nor a theorem proving that cohort-time latent ATTs remain invariant over that extension fiber.
fill: Prove the general-grid necessity-and-sufficiency theorem with explicit zero-capacity conventions and one joint potential-outcome construction; then prove the root-free counterfactual subdistribution and sharp observed-grid ATT formula. Exact five-date twins and root-exclusion examples will serve as nontriviality and falsification checks, not as substitutes for the proof.
